# SPEC — Zen 2030 Document Management & Workflow

## Summary
Zen 2030 Slice-1 is a desktop-first, Italian-language document management and validation platform for 5 named users, 20 GB initial storage, and up to 600 documents per month. It must support upload of PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG files; OCR and field extraction; human validation; minimal task workflow; searchable archive; controlled export; and validated-only generative summary and Q&A.
The pilot delivery profile is AWS in an EU region, but the solution must preserve the same business behavior on approved on-prem infrastructure. Profile differences are limited to infrastructure adapters such as object storage, queue/event transport, secret provider, observability sinks, runtime platform, and GPU serving environment.

## Goals
- Deliver a demo-ready Slice-1 within 2 weeks, targeting 10 effective working days.
- Reduce manual data entry by at least 50% per document through automated pre-fill of key fields.
- Achieve at least 85% first-pass extraction accuracy on key fields in pilot scope.
- Ensure no document reaches the Validated state without explicit human confirmation.
- Provide metadata and full-text search with document open within 30 seconds in 90% of cases.
- Preserve a complete audit trail for upload, correction, validation, export, and AI query access where applicable.
- Maintain functional parity across AWS and on-prem deployment profiles for all Slice-1 business capabilities.
- Provide validated-only generative summary and Q&A with citations and no autonomous business action.

## Non-Goals
- Replacing ERP, CRM, PEC, accounting, or HR systems.
- Implementing full accounting approval, payment automation, or advanced workflow orchestration.
- Bulk historical backfile ingestion or historical cleanup.
- Supporting multiple workflows per document family in Slice-1.
- Providing electronic signature, legal preservation, protocol, legal hold, or formal records retention procedures.
- Delivering a native mobile app, offline mode, multi-tenant support, or multi-company support.
- Adding predictive analytics, advanced auto-routing, or autonomous generative actions.
- Hardening for extreme enterprise-scale workloads beyond pilot targets.

## Users & Context
- Primary user: administrative or document operator using a web dashboard to upload, review extracted fields, correct data, validate documents, search archives, and export files.
- Secondary stakeholders: IT for platform, access, and operations; Finance or Administration for audit and controls; DPO and Compliance for personal data and retention; HR as a future extension.
- Operating context: desktop-first back-office web application in Italian, notifications via dashboard and email, throughput up to 50 documents per day burst and 7,200 documents per year baseline.
- Deployment context: AWS-first pilot delivery in EU region with equivalent on-prem support; business APIs, lifecycle semantics, RBAC semantics, audit semantics, and operator-visible workflow behavior must remain unchanged across profiles.
- Accessibility context: WCAG requirements are not explicitly defined and must not block Slice-1 unless later required.

## Functional Requirements
- FR-1 Document Intake
  - The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG files up to 20 MB through a web upload flow.
  - The system shall acknowledge upload and assign a unique document identifier.
  - The system shall retain the original file in profile-specific object storage through an adapter contract.
- FR-2 Processing
  - The system shall parse supported digital formats and run OCR on scanned inputs.
  - The system shall classify documents using configurable rules and optional model-based extraction where available.
  - The system shall extract key pilot-scope fields and store a confidence score per extracted field.
  - The system shall place documents with parse or OCR failures into an operator-visible exception state with a readable reason.
- FR-3 Validation Workspace
  - The system shall provide one operator workspace showing document preview, extracted fields, confidence scores, provenance needed for correction, and current workflow state.
  - The system shall allow manual correction of extracted fields before validation.
  - The system shall preserve original value, corrected value, actor, and timestamp for each correction.
  - The system shall require explicit human confirmation before transition to Validated.
- FR-4 Workflow and Tasks
  - The system shall create an assignable task after processing for each uploaded document.
  - The system shall support one validation-oriented workflow only in Slice-1.
  - The system shall expose dashboard notifications and optionally email notifications when a document becomes validation-ready or enters exception.
- FR-5 Archive and Retrieval
  - The system shall archive the original file, extracted text, metadata, and lifecycle history for each document.
  - The system shall support search by key metadata fields in scope and full-text search over extracted content.
  - The system shall provide preview and controlled download subject to RBAC.
- FR-6 Export
  - The system shall allow authorized users to export a document and its relevant metadata or audit-relevant package as defined in Slice-1.
  - The system shall record export activity in the audit trail.
- FR-7 Generative Assistant
  - The system shall provide summary and Q&A only over validated documents.
  - The system shall show citations or references to supporting passages in responses.
  - The system shall not modify metadata, workflow state, or business records through AI responses.
- FR-8 Security and Access
  - The system shall integrate with OIDC and/or SAML for user authentication.
  - The system shall enforce RBAC using application roles or IdP groups.
  - The system shall externalize MFA policy to the IdP.
- FR-9 Deployment Parity
  - The system shall preserve the same business APIs and lifecycle semantics across AWS and on-prem profiles.
  - The system shall isolate profile-specific infrastructure behind adapters for storage, queue/eventing, secrets, observability, and AI runtime.

## Non-Functional Requirements
- Performance
  - P95 upload acknowledgment shall be below 5 seconds for files up to 20 MB.
  - P95 search response shall be below 2 seconds.
  - Search and open of an archived document shall complete within 30 seconds in 90% of cases.
  - P95 generative answer latency shall be at or below 20 seconds for one validated document up to 20 pages.
- Throughput
  - The system shall support 600 documents per month with burst handling around 50 documents per day.
- Availability and Recovery
  - Pilot availability target shall be 99.5% during working hours.
  - Recovery objectives shall be RPO 60 minutes and RTO 240 minutes.
- Security
  - Data shall be encrypted at rest and in transit.
  - Internet egress shall remain restricted to approved endpoints.
  - PII shall be minimized in logs and redacted where present.
- Compliance
  - Data residency shall remain within approved EU deployment profiles.
  - Auditability shall cover upload, correction, validation, export, and AI query access where applicable.
- Quality
  - Backend quality gates shall target at least 80% coverage with clean lint, type, security, and build checks.
  - Frontend quality gates shall target at least 75% coverage with clean lint, type, and build checks.
  - AI/RAG quality gates shall target at least 70% coverage with clean lint, security, and build checks.
- Portability
  - AWS and on-prem profiles shall preserve functional parity and unchanged business contracts.
- UX
  - The operator experience shall remain simple and transparent with one upload flow and guided correction-oriented validation.

## High-Level Architecture
- Frontend: Next.js 14 web application for upload, validation, task inbox, archive search, export initiation, and AI access.
- Backend: FastAPI services for business APIs, workflow orchestration, validation, audit, export, profile adapters, and integration with document core.
- Document core: Paperless-ngx plus parsing and OCR pipeline using Apache Tika, Unstructured, Tesseract, and PaddleOCR/docTR as configured.
- Data layer: PostgreSQL 16 for metadata, workflow, audit, and pgvector; Redis-compatible cache; S3-compatible object storage for originals and derived artifacts.
- Messaging and events: queue and event transport resolved by deployment profile.
- AI layer: self-hosted inference in approved EU profile with validated-only retrieval, embeddings using bge-m3, and reranking using bge-reranker.
- Identity and access: OIDC and/or SAML with RBAC from application groups or IdP groups.
- Observability: structured logs, OpenTelemetry traces, and Prometheus-compatible metrics with profile-specific sinks.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[Operator] --> FE[Next.js Web App]
  FE --> API[FastAPI Business API]
  API --> WF[Workflow and Task Service]
  API --> DOC[Paperless-ngx and Processing Orchestrator]
  DOC --> PARSE[Apache Tika / Unstructured]
  DOC --> OCR[Tesseract / PaddleOCR / docTR]
  API --> DB[(PostgreSQL + pgvector)]
  API --> CACHE[(Redis-compatible Cache)]
  API --> OBJ[(S3-compatible Object Storage)]
  API --> MSG[Queue / Event Adapter]
  API --> AUTH[OIDC / SAML IdP]
  API --> AI[Validated-only RAG Service]
  AI --> DB
  AI --> OBJ
  API --> OBS[OpenTelemetry / Metrics / Logs]
```

## Interfaces
- User Interface
  - Web dashboard for upload, preview, correction, validation, task inbox, search, export, and AI Q&A.
- Business API
  - REST APIs for document intake, document detail, validation actions, task list and assignment, search, export initiation, and AI query over validated documents.
  - API contracts shall remain profile-independent across AWS and on-prem.
- Internal Processing Interfaces
  - Adapter interface for object storage.
  - Adapter interface for queue and event transport.
  - Adapter interface for secret provider.
  - Adapter interface for observability sinks.
  - Adapter interface for AI runtime serving.
- Identity Interface
  - OIDC and/or SAML integration with external IdP.
- Notification Interface
  - Dashboard notifications mandatory.
  - Email notifications optional when SMTP or equivalent channel is available or responsibly mocked.
- Repository Evidence Constraint
  - Implementation decisions were informed by the local source snapshot and project artifacts provided for this run.

## Data Model (logical)
### Entity: User
- id: UUID/string — unique user identifier from application or IdP mapping
- username: string — unique within deployment profile
- display_name: string — operator-readable name
- role: enum — RBAC role
- idp_group_refs: string[] — source groups for authorization
- active: boolean — access enabled flag

### Entity: Document
- id: UUID — primary identifier assigned at intake
- original_filename: string — user-provided file name
- media_type: string — detected or declared content type
- format: enum — pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, jpg, png
- size_bytes: integer — maximum 20 MB for Slice-1 intake
- storage_uri: string — object storage locator through adapter
- extracted_text_uri: string|null — derived text artifact locator
- classification_label: string|null — pilot-scope document class
- state: enum — uploaded, processing, validation_ready, exception, validated, exported
- uploaded_by: UUID/string — reference to User
- uploaded_at: datetime — intake timestamp
- validated_by: UUID/string|null — reference to User
- validated_at: datetime|null — explicit validation timestamp

### Entity: ExtractedField
- id: UUID — primary identifier
- document_id: UUID — reference to Document
- field_name: string — pilot-scope metadata key
- proposed_value: string|null — system-extracted value
- confidence_score: decimal — 0 to 1 or equivalent normalized score
- corrected_value: string|null — operator-confirmed value
- provenance: string|null — extraction source or passage reference where available
- status: enum — proposed, corrected, accepted, rejected
- updated_by: UUID/string|null — actor for last change
- updated_at: datetime — last modification timestamp

### Entity: Task
- id: UUID — primary identifier
- document_id: UUID — reference to Document
- task_type: enum — validation
- assignee_id: UUID/string|null — assigned operator
- status: enum — open, in_progress, completed, exception
- created_at: datetime — task creation timestamp
- updated_at: datetime — task state update timestamp
- due_at: datetime|null — optional operational target

### Entity: AuditEvent
- id: UUID — primary identifier
- document_id: UUID|null — related document where applicable
- actor_id: UUID/string|null — user or service identity
- event_type: enum — upload, parse, ocr, classify, correct, validate, notify, search, export, ai_query, exception
- before_value: json/null — prior state snapshot where relevant
- after_value: json/null — resulting state snapshot where relevant
- reason: string|null — human-readable rationale or exception reason
- created_at: datetime — immutable event timestamp

### Entity: Notification
- id: UUID — primary identifier
- user_id: UUID/string — target user
- document_id: UUID|null — related document
- channel: enum — dashboard, email
- notification_type: enum — validation_ready, exception, export_ready
- status: enum — pending, sent, failed, read
- created_at: datetime — creation timestamp
- sent_at: datetime|null — delivery timestamp

### Entity: ExportJob
- id: UUID — primary identifier
- requested_by: UUID/string — requesting user
- document_id: UUID — related document
- status: enum — requested, running, completed, failed
- output_uri: string|null — export artifact location
- created_at: datetime — request timestamp
- completed_at: datetime|null — finish timestamp

### Entity: AIQuery
- id: UUID — primary identifier
- document_id: UUID — must reference a validated document
- requested_by: UUID/string — requesting user
- query_text: string — user question
- response_text: string|null — generated answer
- citations: json — supporting passage references
- status: enum — requested, completed, denied, failed
- created_at: datetime — request timestamp
- completed_at: datetime|null — completion timestamp

## Key Workflows
- Upload to Validation
  - Operator uploads a supported file.
  - System acknowledges upload, stores original file, creates Document in uploaded state, and emits processing work.
  - Processing pipeline parses content, runs OCR if needed, classifies document, extracts fields, and records confidence scores.
  - System creates a validation task and notification when document becomes validation_ready, or exception with readable reason if processing fails.
  - Operator reviews preview and extracted fields, corrects values if needed, and explicitly validates.
- Search and Retrieval
  - Authorized user searches by metadata field or full text.
  - System returns ordered results.
  - User opens preview and optionally downloads original file under RBAC.
- Export
  - Authorized user requests export from document view or results list.
  - System creates ExportJob, produces output package, and records audit event.
- Validated-only AI Query
  - Authorized user opens AI assistant from a validated document context.
  - System verifies document state is validated before retrieval.
  - RAG service returns summary or answer with citations.
  - System records AI query access in audit without altering lifecycle state.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant O as Operator
  participant UI as Web UI
  participant API as FastAPI
  participant P as Processing
  participant DB as PostgreSQL
  participant A as Audit

  O->>UI: Upload file
  UI->>API: Create document intake
  API->>DB: Save Document(uploaded)
  API->>A: Record upload event
  API->>P: Enqueue processing
  P->>DB: Save extracted fields and state
  P->>A: Record parse/OCR/classify events
  P->>DB: Create validation task
  O->>UI: Review preview and fields
  UI->>API: Submit corrections and validate
  API->>DB: Save corrections and state(validated)
  API->>A: Record correct and validate events
```

## Security & Compliance
- GDPR applies to Slice-1.
- Data must remain in approved EU deployment profiles only.
- Authentication must use OIDC and/or SAML with MFA policy externalized to the IdP.
- Authorization must use RBAC with roles derived from application groups or IdP groups.
- Encryption at rest and in transit is mandatory.
- Internet egress must remain restricted to approved internal services and approved regional infrastructure services.
- Logs must use structured logging with PII redaction and no unredacted prompt logging.
- AI access must be limited to validated documents only.
- Audit trail must support reconstruction of who uploaded, corrected, validated, exported, or queried a document.
- Retention baseline is 3,650 days for transactional data and 180 days for logs, subject to legal confirmation before go-live.
- Sensitive document categories, exact retention rules, and legal preservation requirements remain to be confirmed and are not part of Slice-1 delivery.

## Deployment & Operations
- Delivery profiles
  - Primary pilot profile: AWS app core plus AWS AI runtime in an EU region.
  - Supported equivalent profile: approved on-prem containers or Kubernetes plus approved on-prem GPU runtime.
- Runtime
  - Containerized Linux services using Python 3.12 and Node 20.
  - Portable runtime profiles must keep business contracts unchanged.
- Core components
  - Next.js 14 frontend, FastAPI backend, Paperless-ngx document core, PostgreSQL 16, Redis-compatible cache, S3-compatible object storage.
- Profile-specific adapters
  - AWS: S3, SQS, SNS, AWS Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, AWS GPU runtime.
  - On-prem: S3-compatible object storage, approved queue, approved event transport, Vault or approved secret store, centralized logs, approved GPU runtime.
- Operations
  - CI/CD via GitHub Actions with CI and CD workflows indicated in project constraints.
  - Security scanning via Trivy with zero critical vulnerabilities allowed by default profile.
  - Observability shall include metrics for ingest, OCR, workflow, search, export, and AI paths, plus end-to-end tracing.
  - Backup and recovery shall align to RPO 60 minutes and RTO 240 minutes.
- Pilot support assumptions
  - SMTP or equivalent email channel may be real or responsibly mocked for pilot.
  - An existing IdP is preferred; Keycloak is acceptable only if approved.

## Risks & Mitigations
- Risk: Paperless-ngx may not cover validation workflow, audit, export, or AI control needs end-to-end.
  - Mitigation: keep Paperless-ngx as document core and implement missing business capabilities in FastAPI services with explicit contracts.
- Risk: OCR and extraction accuracy may fall below 85% due to poor input quality.
  - Mitigation: use real sample documents early, expose confidence scores, and route failures to exception handling and human correction.
- Risk: Operators may distrust AI suggestions and validation may slow down.
  - Mitigation: show confidence scores, field provenance where available, clear correction microcopy, and require explicit human validation.
- Risk: AWS-specific decisions may break on-prem portability.
  - Mitigation: define adapter contracts early and keep business APIs, lifecycle semantics, and RBAC semantics profile-independent.
- Risk: Retention rules and sensitive document classes are not fully confirmed.
  - Mitigation: implement configurable retention metadata and block go-live decisions on legal/compliance confirmation rather than pilot demo delivery.
- Risk: Email, IdP, or approved on-prem target may be unavailable during pilot window.
  - Mitigation: support optional email, allow responsible mocking where approved, and keep authentication integration configurable.
- Risk: AI runtime or GPU capacity may delay validated-only Q&A.
  - Mitigation: keep AI service isolated, self-hosted, and profile-driven; prioritize core ingest and validation if capacity is constrained.

## Assumptions
- Real sample documents are available for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and scanned image inputs.
- AWS account access in an approved EU region is available for the pilot.
- An approved on-prem target standard exists or will be provided for parity verification.
- SMTP or equivalent email capability exists or may be responsibly mocked.
- An enterprise IdP exists, or Keycloak is approved as an alternative.
- Pilot-scope key fields and document category priorities will be confirmed from real samples during implementation.
- WCAG requirements are not formalized for Slice-1 and therefore are not release-blocking unless later required.
- Export package shape is limited to Slice-1 needs and does not imply formal records management compliance.
- The local repository snapshot and provided artifacts may inform implementation decisions, but no GitHub remote verification was performed in this run.

## Success Metrics
- TTFA from login to first validated document at or below 10 minutes.
- At least 85% of upload to validation to search tasks completed without assistance.
- Critical error rate at or below 2% per ingest or validation operation.
- First-pass extraction accuracy at or above 85% on key pilot-scope fields.
- Search-to-open time at or below 30 seconds in 90% of cases.
- Idea-to-demo lead time at or below 10 calendar days.
- Pilot CSAT at or above 4.2/5 across the initial user group.
- Active usage by at least 3 of 5 pilot users for go/no-go consideration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a supported file in PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, or PNG format up to 20 MB, when an operator uploads it, then the system returns an acknowledgment with a unique document identifier within P95 5 seconds and stores the document in uploaded state.
- Given a document that completes parsing and OCR, when extraction runs on pilot-scope fields, then the system stores a proposed value and confidence score for each extracted field and reaches at least 85% first-pass accuracy on the agreed pilot sample set.
- Given a document with processing failure, when parsing or OCR cannot complete, then the document is visible in an exception state with a readable reason in the operator dashboard and no hidden terminal failure occurs.
- Given a document in validation_ready state, when an operator opens the validation workspace, then the UI shows document preview, extracted fields, confidence scores, and workflow state in one workspace and allows correction before validation.
- Given any document not yet explicitly confirmed by a human, when a user attempts to mark it as Validated through UI or API, then the transition is rejected unless explicit human confirmation is recorded with actor and timestamp.
- Given a corrected extracted field, when the operator saves the correction, then the system preserves original value, corrected value, actor, and timestamp in persistent audit history retrievable by an authorized user.
- Given an authorized user searches by invoice number, supplier, VAT number, or full text over archived content, when the query matches stored metadata or extracted text, then the system returns ordered results within P95 2 seconds and allows preview or download according to RBAC.
- Given a validated document, when an authorized user requests summary or Q&A, then the AI service answers within P95 20 seconds for a document up to 20 pages, includes citations to supporting passages, and does not change metadata or lifecycle state.
- Given equivalent AWS and on-prem deployments with profile-specific adapters configured, when the same business API and operator workflow are executed, then document lifecycle semantics, task lifecycle semantics, RBAC behavior, audit behavior, and validated-only AI access rules remain unchanged.
- Given pilot operating hours, when the platform is measured over the pilot period, then availability is at least 99.5%, backup and recovery capability meets RPO 60 minutes and RTO 240 minutes, and logs contain structured audit-relevant events with PII redaction.

## Out Of Scope
- Third-party integrations with ERP, CRM, PEC, accounting, or HR systems.
- Historical bulk ingestion, backfile remediation, or legacy repository cleanup.
- More than one workflow per document family.
- Electronic signature, legal preservation, protocol, legal hold, or formal records retention procedures.
- Native mobile applications, offline mode, multi-tenancy, or multi-company support.
- Advanced analytics, predictive routing, or autonomous AI-driven business actions.
- Enterprise-wide scale optimization beyond 5 named users, 20 GB, and 600 documents per month for Slice-1.

## Note from Harper Orchestrator (Super User) to be applied
- Preserve outcome-first scope: ingest, OCR/IDP, human validation, minimum workflow, archive search, export, and validated-only Q&A.
- Keep AWS as the primary pilot delivery profile, but treat on-prem as a first-class equivalent deployment profile from the start.
- Do not change business contracts or operator-visible behavior between deployment profiles; isolate differences behind runtime adapters.
- Keep human validation mandatory before Validated state.
- Implementation decisions were informed by the local source snapshot and project artifacts provided for this run.

### Acceptance — REQ-001

- Adds canonical PostgreSQL 16 and Alembic backbone for `User`, `Document`, `ExtractedField`, `Task`, `AuditEvent`, `Notification`, `ExportJob`, and `AIQuery`.
- Enforces unique keys and invariants required later: document `id`, username uniqueness per deployment profile, one task type `validation`, and immutable audit event identifiers.
- Defines document lifecycle explicitly: initial `uploaded`; allowed `uploaded -> processing`, `processing -> validation_ready`, `processing -> exception`, `validation_ready -> validated`; all other direct transitions rejected.
- Defines `Document.state = exported` as reserved in schema but forbidden in Slice-1 transitions, so export does not break validated-only AI eligibility.
- Defines extracted field lifecycle explicitly: `proposed -> corrected`, `proposed -> accepted`, `proposed -> rejected`, `corrected -> accepted`; direct `rejected -> accepted` is forbidden.
- Defines task lifecycle explicitly: `open -> in_progress -> completed` and `open|in_progress -> exception`; `completed` requires related document already `validated`.
- Defines notification lifecycle explicitly: `pending -> sent|failed` and `sent -> read`; `read -> pending` is forbidden.
- Defines export job lifecycle explicitly: `requested -> running -> completed|failed`; defines AI query lifecycle explicitly: `requested -> completed|denied|failed`.
- Creates search-supporting indexes for metadata fields in pilot scope and full-text search over extracted text references without embedding raw document blobs in PostgreSQL.
- Migration tests verify upgrade and downgrade on empty and seeded databases and prove audit tables preserve created timestamps and immutable rows.

### Acceptance — REQ-002

- Normalizes OIDC and or SAML identity assertions into a stable actor context containing user id, display name, active flag, and permission set derived from application groups or IdP groups.
- Exposes a profile-independent authorization primitive so all later business commands check permissions rather than hard-coded usernames or profile-specific logic.
- Returns `401` for unauthenticated requests and `403` for authenticated but unauthorized requests, with no document, task, export, or AI mutation.
- Records actor identifiers on accepted write operations and preserves that actor in downstream audit events created by later REQs.
- Deny responses are deterministic and do not leak group names, token contents, secret references, or internal adapter details.
- Structured logs contain stable request and actor correlation identifiers while redacting tokens, assertions, and personal data beyond minimum identifiers.
- Provides deterministic non-production test identity fixtures so `/kit` and `/eval` can exercise allow and deny paths without a live IdP.

### Acceptance — REQ-003

- Accepts only PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG uploads up to 20 MB through a business API protected by upload permission.
- Returns an acknowledgment with a unique document identifier and persisted `uploaded` state within the Slice-1 P95 target of 5 seconds for accepted files.
- Persists original filename, media type, format, size, uploader identity, upload timestamp, and object storage locator through the storage adapter contract.
- Emits one processing request event per accepted document and never performs hidden in-request OCR or extraction work.
- Creates an immutable upload audit event with actor, timestamp, document id, and storage outcome metadata.
- Rejects unsupported media types, oversize files, and malformed multipart input with explicit client-visible reasons and no partial document row left behind.
- If object storage write fails, the request fails atomically, no processing event is emitted, and no orphaned audit or document records remain.

### Acceptance — REQ-004

- Consumes intake requests idempotently and transitions documents `uploaded -> processing` only when the worker actually starts handling them.
- Parses supported digital formats, runs OCR for scanned inputs, applies configurable classification rules, and persists extracted text location plus pilot-scope extracted fields.
- Persists one `ExtractedField` row per extracted key with proposed value, normalized confidence score, provenance when available, and status `proposed`.
- Transitions documents `processing -> validation_ready` on successful extraction or `processing -> exception` on parse OCR classify failure with a readable operator reason.
- Writes immutable audit events for parse, OCR, classify, extraction success, and exception outcomes, including machine actor and timestamps.
- Duplicate delivery of the same processing event does not create duplicate extracted fields or duplicate terminal state transitions.
- Processing failures do not silently terminate; every terminal failure produces persisted exception reason visible to later UI and task flows.

### Acceptance — REQ-005

- Creates exactly one validation task per processed document when processing reaches a terminal outcome relevant to operators.
- For `validation_ready`, creates a task in `open` status; for `exception`, creates or updates the related task in `exception` status with the same readable reason.
- Supports assignment and work progress transitions using the canonical task lifecycle without introducing a second workflow family.
- Creates a mandatory dashboard notification for validation-ready and exception outcomes and an email notification only when an approved email adapter is configured.
- Notification state changes are explicit: created as `pending`, marked `sent` when delivered to dashboard or email channel, and later `read` only by user action.
- Optional email absence does not fail the document workflow; dashboard notification remains authoritative for pilot behavior.
- Emits audit events for task creation, assignment change when implemented, notification creation, and notification delivery failure when email was attempted.

## Scope

REQ-003 implements the document intake upload command for the Zen2030 document workflow platform. It accepts supported file uploads (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, PNG) up to 20 MB, persists a document record in `uploaded` state, stores the original file through a storage adapter contract, emits one `processing_requested` event, and writes one immutable `upload` audit event per accepted upload.
